channel.title: Digital Health & AI in Medicine
channel.description: Posts and perspectives on AI, medicine and the future of healthcare.

item.title: AMIE prepares patients before the appointment
item.description: 98 completed visits; clinicians found AMIE helpful for preparation in 33 of 44 reviewed cases. An early supervised feasibility study, not proof of better clinical outcomes.

item.title: AI takes on research-level physics
item.description: My take on what research-level physics results could mean for the pace of discovery.

item.title: Healthcare waste, seen through art
item.description: A hospital artwork in Istanbul prompted thoughts about waste and resources in healthcare.

item.title: Die langweilige AI-Revolution
item.description: The biggest early gains may come from less documentation, better coordination and more time for patients.

item.title: When a watch gets new medical capabilities
item.description: What a Pixel Watch update suggests about the speed, scale and business models of digital health.

item.title: Private weekend care and the price of access
item.description: A private weekend service in Linz raises questions about access, working conditions and the erosion of publicly funded care.

item.title: iPatient versus iDoctor
item.description: A critical look at AI plans, remote consultations and the risk that efficiency makes care less personal.

item.title: Revisiting the AI 2027 scenario
item.description: A reflection on AI scenarios and reports about autonomous model behaviour. Scenarios are not forecasts or clinical evidence.

item.title: The heart has a blue screen of death. AI learns to predict it.
item.description: A look at AI, sudden cardiac arrest and the questions this raises for MedTech.

item.title: Hospital cooling is more than a household problem
item.description: Why criticism of hot hospitals should consider building rules, financing, infection control and operating-room ventilation.

item.title: Health-Daten: Mitten im medizinischen Souveränitätsverlust
item.description: Why control over health data matters for clinical care, digital independence and a European health-AI ecosystem.

item.title: AI diagnostics and the challenge of real life
item.description: My post on how incomplete information and real-world conditions can challenge strong benchmark results.

item.title: What GKV reform could mean for providers and MedTech
item.description: My analysis of the commission recommendations and their implications for clinics, practices, manufacturers and evidence requirements.

item.title: Hybrid DRGs and the shift toward outpatient care
item.description: My analysis of reimbursement incentives, hospital stays and opportunities for outpatient providers.

item.title: The concentration of healthcare costs at the end of life
item.description: A look at the concentration of healthcare spending near the end of life and the questions this raises for care.

item.title: Wenn der Patient die Route kennt: Der „Google-Maps-Moment“ der Medizin
item.description: How patient-facing AI may change the doctor-patient relationship, preparation for consultations and the role of clinical judgement.

item.title: A paid AI product is not automatically a leading model
item.description: A podcast prompted me to question the gap between enterprise AI branding, model choice and perceived capability.

item.title: Roomba and the cost of losing customer focus
item.description: A reflection on product decisions, customer needs and the tensions between capital-market priorities and useful technology.

item.title: AI changes the link between growth and hiring
item.description: AI may change the assumption that business growth requires a proportional increase in headcount, with robotics potentially following.

item.title: mRNA vaccines and cancer immunotherapy
item.description: My reaction to a study exploring how mRNA vaccination may interact with cancer immunotherapy.
